You are a data scientist for a mid-sized business, in a small group of 3-4 data scientists. You’ve been tasked with creating a report evaluating a scenario for your business. Your colleagues will also be evaluating the same scenario, and your reports will be used in aggregate to determine a consensus (or lack thereof) on the company’s action. The reports will also be used to inform downsizing that is rumored to be coming - you want to ensure your report is better than your peers so that you aren’t as easy to cut.
You may talk to your peers who are assigned the same scenario, but you do not want to collaborate too closely, lest you both become targets of the rumored layoffs.

title: Appendix B — Draft: Results
text:
Data Characteristics
The bridge condition data was collected from the National Bridge Inventory dataset provided by the Federal Highway Administration (“Download NBI ASCII Files - National Bridge Inventory - Bridge Inspection - Safety Inspection - Bridges & Structures - Federal Highway Administration” n.d.). This dataset has information about brdige age, the structural condition, and also the overall bridge ratings.
The bridges condition is measured by three things, deck, superstructure, and substructure ratings. These ratings are on a scale from 0 to 9. Higher numbers mean the bridge is in better condition. The dataset also include a sufficiency rating. This ranges from 0 to 100 and gives the bridge an overall score.
Information about repairs and bridge management was also taken from the Nebraska Department of Transportation bridge reports (“Bridge - NDOT” n.d.). Traffic data was taken from Federal highway Administration, which includes estimates of how many vehicles use a brdige each day (“Highway Statistics 2023 - Policy Federal Highway Administration” n.d.).
Inclusion Criteria: The only bridges that were included are the ones located in the Omaha metropolitan area with complete structural condition ratings. Any bridges missing any ratings were not included.

title: Appendix B — Draft: Results
text:
Primary Analysis: Probability of Failure
The probability of bridge failure was estimated by using the structural condition ratings matched with the bridge age. Bridges with lower ratings or lower sufficiency scores are high risk.
Older Bridges tend to have lower sufficiency scores. This suggests gradual deterioration over time. Most bridges however, are still in good condition. Some do have lower scores that could lead to a higher risk of problems in their structure.

title: Appendix B — Draft: Results
text:
Secondary Analysis: Consequences of Failure
Traffic volume and planned maintenance were examined to estimate the potential consequences of a bridge collapse. Bridges that have a higher volume of cars each day would cause a lot more disruption if they failed.
Some bridges already have repairs planned or in the planning according to NDOT reports. This could help reduce near-term risk. Brdiges that carry high daily traffic and also have low sufficiency scores are the highest overall risk.

Calculation of Bridge Risk
Overall bridge risk combines the probability of failure and the consequences of failure:
Risk = Probability of Failure × Consequence of Failure

Key findings/Conclusion
Some key findings that were found was that most bridges are in fair to good condition. Only about 12% are actually in poor condition and need monitoring or repair. Next key finding is older bridges tend to have lower sufficiency ratings due to gradual deterioration. Also bridges with high traffic volumes would cause the biggest disruptions if they were to collapse. In conclusion, widespread bridge failure is unlikely, but targeted monitoring and maintence of lowe-rated brdiges is recommened over the nect five years to help reduce over risk of bridge failure.

title: Appendix D — Draft: Executive Summary
text:
This report evaluates the risk of a bridge collapsing in Omaha, Nebraska over the nest five years. The goal of this report is to help the people that make decisions for the city understand the current risks and identify actions that can help reduce those risks.
Data from the National Bridge Inventory, Nebraska Department of Transportation, and federal traffic statistics were used to help analyze bridge condition, age, traffic levels, and planned maintenance. Risk was defined as the mixture of the probability of failure and the consequences if a failure does occur.
The analysis shows that most of the bridges in Omaha are in fair to good condition currently. However, there are a couple of bridges that have lower condition ratings which means they are more at risk. The older bridges were more likely to have slightly lower condition scores, suggesting that deterioration over time is also an important factor.
Traffic data shows that some bridges carry much higher volumes of vehicles then others. So, if one of these high traffic bridges were to fail, it would cause a lot of disruption to the traffic flow and could also hurt people. Bridges that have the lower condition ratings and high traffic levels are the greatest risk.
Overall, the risk of all bridges collapsing is very low in Omaha. However, there are certain bridges that need more attention to prevent problems in the future.

Recommendations

Increase monitoring of older bridges with low condition scores
Start and prioritize repairs for bridges in bad condition
Continue regular inspections/maintenance
Focus more on high traffic bridges where failure would cause greatest impact

Taking these steps will help reduce the chance of bridges failing and also the potential problems that could happen if failure occurs.

title: Appendix C — Draft: Intro/Conclusions
text:
Introduction
Bridge safety has become a bigger concern over the recent year. The reason is because some bridges have collapsed and caused many problems in other parts of the country. Due to this, cities are starting to pay more attention to how safe their infrastructure actually is.
If anyone has driven through Omaha they understand how important bridges are for daily traffic, especially on major roads like I-80. If a bridge were to fail, it could cause serious problems for both safety and transportation.
The goal of this report is to estimate the risk of a bridge collapse in Omaha over the next five years. This is done by looking at bridge condition, age, traffic levels, and maintenance data from public sources.


Conclusion
Overall, most bridges in Omaha are in decent condition, so the risk of a collapse is not very high. However, there are some bridges that have lower condition ratings and could be a concern.
Bridges that are older and carry a lot more traffic would cause the biggest problems if something were to go wrong. Due to this, it’s important to keep a close watch on these bridges and make repairs on them when needed.
In the future, using more detailed data or better models could help improve these estimates. However, for now, focusing on maintenance and monitoring is the best way to reduce the risk of a collapse.
